data.narrative:
Stardust Solutions is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Yanai Yedvab that has raised $75M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a peer universe of nine private-sector climate and energy companies, including later-stage players like Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, alongside one public comparable (LNZA).

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($75M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $150M. The peer-median method is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables in the narrow climate and energy cohort—while nine sector peers exist, fewer than three met tighter filtering criteria around stage and valuation tier, making a median calculation unreliable and sector-wide aggregation potentially misleading.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $128M to $172M, with a median point of $150M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.0x multiplier for Stardust's specific subsector positioning within climate and energy, the quality of available exit and Series B funding data for comparable companies, and potential differences in capital efficiency or technological risk relative to the peer set. A broader set of same-stage or recently-funded comparables would strengthen confidence in this range.
